preconditions.description: Input consists of two integers n (number of people) and k (number of imbalanced people), where n is between 1 and 100,000 inclusive, and k is between 0 and n inclusive.
The input is exactly two space-separated integers n and k.

postconditions.description: If no valid construction exists, output is exactly 'NO'. Otherwise, output is 'YES' followed by exactly n integers (s_1, ..., s_n) representing the child of each person (0 ≤ s_i ≤ n).

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(s_i) <= int(n) for s_i in stdout.strip().split()[1:]) if stdout.strip().startswith('YES') else True
postconditions.description: If output starts with 'YES', the following n integers must each be between 0 and n inclusive.

postconditions.expression: any(int(s_i) == 0 for s_i in stdout.strip().split()[1:]) if stdout.strip().startswith('YES') else True
postconditions.description: If output starts with 'YES', exactly one person has no child (s_i = 0).

postconditions.expression: (stdout.strip().startswith('YES') and sum(1 for i in range(1, int(n) + 1) if is_imbalanced(i, stdout.strip().split()[1:])) == int(k)) or stdout.strip() == 'NO'
postconditions.description: If output starts with 'YES', the constructed genealogy must have exactly k imbalanced people, where a person i is imbalanced if they have both parents and one parent's ancestor count is at least double the other's. The function is_imbalanced(i, s) is defined as follows: a person i has both parents if there exist j and l such that s[j] == i and s[l] == i; the ancestor count of a person x is the number of distinct ancestors (including themselves) in the genealogy.
